questions.text: Which of the following BEST describes the concept of "accountability" in quality management?

options.a: The ability to shift responsibility for quality to frontline staff only
options.b: The clear assignment of responsibility for quality outcomes with mechanisms for follow-through and reporting
options.c: The process of reporting errors to external regulatory agencies only
options.d: A punitive system for identifying underperforming departments

questions.explanation: Accountability in quality means clearly defining who is responsible for what quality outcomes and ensuring mechanisms are in place to track performance, report results, and follow through on improvements.

questions.text: An organization is preparing for an accreditation survey and conducts a mock survey. The PRIMARY purpose of a mock survey is to:

options.a: Train staff to give scripted responses to surveyors
options.b: Identify gaps in standards compliance and correct them before the actual survey
options.c: Reduce survey anxiety without changing practices
options.d: Produce a compliance report for the Board of Directors

questions.explanation: Mock surveys simulate actual accreditation surveys to proactively identify compliance gaps, enabling corrective action before the formal survey — improving performance and reducing the risk of deficiency citations.

questions.text: Which of the following BEST describes the relationship between quality improvement and performance management?

options.a: They are entirely separate functions with no overlap
options.b: Performance management uses data to assess outcomes; QI uses that data to drive systematic improvements
options.c: Performance management is a clinical function; QI is an administrative function
options.d: QI replaces performance management in modern healthcare organizations

questions.explanation: Performance management and quality improvement are closely linked — performance management tracks and evaluates outcomes, while QI uses those insights to design and test systematic improvements. They are complementary, not separate.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a "structure" measure in Donabedian's framework?

options.a: Percentage of patients who received discharge instructions
options.b: 30-day readmission rate
options.c: The availability of a dedicated quality improvement team
options.d: Patient satisfaction with communication

questions.explanation: Donabedian's framework includes Structure (resources, facilities, staff), Process (actions taken in providing care), and Outcomes (results of care). A dedicated QI team is a structural resource — it is in place to support quality work.

questions.text: A hospital's quality team is reviewing adverse drug event (ADE) trends. Which of the following is the BEST approach to detect ADEs in medical records?

options.a: Reviewing all physician progress notes for medication references
options.b: Using IHI Global Trigger Tool methodology to screen records for "triggers" that may indicate an ADE
options.c: Relying solely on voluntary incident reporting data
options.d: Auditing pharmacy billing records for high-cost medications

questions.explanation: The IHI Global Trigger Tool uses standardized triggers (e.g., naloxone use, abnormal lab values) to screen records efficiently and identify potential adverse events. Voluntary reporting significantly underestimates ADE rates.

questions.text: Which of the following is the MOST important element of an effective corrective action plan following a quality deficiency?

options.a: A detailed list of all staff members involved in the deficiency
options.b: Clear identification of root causes, specific actions to address them, ownership, and measurable outcome targets
options.c: A legal review of liability exposure
options.d: A financial impact analysis of the deficiency

questions.explanation: An effective CAP addresses root causes (not symptoms), assigns clear ownership for each action, specifies measurable targets, and sets timelines for completion and monitoring — ensuring sustainable improvement.

questions.text: A quality director is asked to demonstrate compliance with TJC Standard LD.03.06.01 related to analyzing quality improvement data. Which of the following BEST fulfills this requirement?

options.a: Submitting patient satisfaction surveys to the Board quarterly
options.b: Establishing a systematic process to compile, analyze, and act on quality and patient safety data across the organization
options.c: Ensuring all staff complete annual quality training
options.d: Conducting patient focus groups twice per year

questions.explanation: TJC LD.03.06.01 requires leaders to use data and information to guide decisions and to systematically analyze and act on quality and patient safety data — requiring an integrated, organization-wide data management and action process.
